arxiv-2204-08618.title: Scalability of gadolinium-doped-water Cherenkov detectors for nuclear nonproliferation
arxiv-2204-08618.creator: Viacheslav A. Li, Steven A. Dazeley, Marc Bergevin, Adam Bernstein
arxiv-2204-08618.description: Abstract Antineutrinos are an unavoidable byproduct of the fission process. The kiloton-scale KamLAND experiment has demonstrated the capability to detect reactor antineutrinos at few-hundred-km range. But to detect or rule out the existence of a single small reactor over many km requires a large detector.

arxiv-2210-14902.title: Characteristic Functions for Cosmological Cross-Correlations 2022 Characteristic Functions for Cosmological Cross-Correlations – 13
arxiv-2210-14902.creator: Patrick C. Breysse, Dongwoo T. Chung, Håvard T. Ihle
arxiv-2210-14902.description: Abstract We introduce a novel unbiased, cross-correlation estimator for the one-point statistics of cosmological random fields. One-point statistics are a useful tool for analysis of highly non-Gaussian density fields, while cross-correlations provide a powerful method for combining information from pairs of fields and separating them from noise and systematics.

arxiv-2409-20422.title: Study of Resonance Production using Run 3 pp Collisions with ALICE
arxiv-2409-20422.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by *. Recent measurements in small collision systems at the LHC show striking similarities between high multiplicity pp, p–Pb collisions and Pb–Pb collisions. In particular, study of hadronic resonances provide valuable information about the final state hadronic interactions. Due to their short lifetime, resonances decay inside the hadronic medium after the chemical freezeout and their decay daughters interact elastically with other hadrons. As a consequence, measured resonance yields get modified.

arxiv-2504-01030.title: Fair Sufficient Representation Learning
arxiv-2504-01030.creator: Xueyu Zhou \rm{Zhou}, Chun Yin Ip \rm{Ip}, Jian Huang \rm{Huang}
arxiv-2504-01030.description: Abstract The main objective of fair statistical modeling and machine learning is to minimize or eliminate biases that may arise from the data or the model itself, ensuring that predictions and decisions are not unjustly influenced by sensitive attributes such as race, gender, age, or other protected characteristics.

arxiv-2507-19564.title: Consistency and Central Limit Results for the Maximum Likelihood Estimator in the Admixture Model
arxiv-2507-19564.description: Abstract In the Admixture Model, the probability of an individual having a certain number of alleles at a specific marker depends on the allele frequencies in K K ancestral populations and the fraction of the individual’s genome originating from these ancestral populations.

pmc-10497533.title: Multidisciplinary studies with mutated HIV-1 capsid proteins reveal structural mechanisms of lattice stabilization
pmc-10497533.creator: Anna T Gres, Karen A Kirby, William M McFadden, Haijuan Du, Dandan Liu, Chaoyi Xu, Alexander J Bryer, Juan R Perilla, Jiong Shi, Christopher Aiken, Xiaofeng Fu, Peijun Zhang, Ashwanth C Francis, Gregory B Melikyan, Stefan G Sarafianos
pmc-10497533.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). HIV-1 capsid (CA) stability is important for viral replication. E45A and P38A mutations enhance and reduce core stability, thus impairing infectivity. Second-site mutations R132T and T216I rescue infectivity. Capsid lattice stability was studied by solving seven crystal structures (in native background), including P38A, P38A/T216I, E45A, E45A/R132T CA, using molecular dynamics simulations of lattices, cryo-electron microscopy of assemblies, time-resolved imaging of uncoating, biophysical and biochemical characterization of assembly and stability.

pmc-11549503.description: acterized by a high prevalence of patients with (1) anxiety and (2) fatigue/palpitations correlate with postablation MACE.▪It is possible that patients with specific symptoms preablation may be at increased risk for atrial fibrillation–related MACE. Key Findings ▪In our sample, approximately one-third of patients undergoing catheter ablation experienced atrial fibrillation–related major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) 1 year postablation.

pmc-11647258.title: Construction of the prognostic nomogram and treatment recommendation in patients with mixed endometrial carcinoma treated with hysterectomy
pmc-11647258.creator: Luyao Kang, Gaili Ji, Nan Zhang, Jie Meng, Duan Liu, Hongyu Li
pmc-11647258.description: Mixed endometrial carcinomas (MECs) account for approximately 3%–10% of all endometrial carcinomas (ECs). These are defined as a combination of two or more distinct histologic subtypes, with at least one being a type II tumor that constitutes at least 5% of the overall tumor. However, the associated prognostic factors and treatment of MECs remain unclear.

pmc-11860516.title: Is relevant postpartum maternal psychopathology on the prognosis of psychomotor development in infants born after a threatened preterm labour across preschool ages?
pmc-11860516.creator: J Andreu, J Buesa, F Ghosn, A Moreno, L Campos, B Almansa, C Zapata, M Lizarán, N Gómez, A García-Blanco
pmc-11860516.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThreatened preterm labour (TPL) is associated with long-lasting neurodevelopmental challenges, independent of prematurity. For instance, it is known that infants born a TPL show delayed communication and socio-individual skills, regardless of the gestational age at birth.

pmc-12418651.title: TriCAM (NCT02976558) – a randomized controlled pilot study of complementary medicine in allogeneic stem cell transplantation to improve quality of life
pmc-12418651.creator: Ali Behzad, Stefan W Krause, Andreas Mackensen, Fabian Müller, Anja Stark, Simon Völkl, Wolf Rösler
pmc-12418651.description: BackgroundAllogeneic stem cell transplantation (aSCT) frequently leads to prolonged impaired quality of life (Qol) and depression. To reduce symptom burden and improve Qol, we implemented a complementary medicine approach (TriCAM).MethodsIn a randomized, controlled clinical trial (NCT02976558), we enrolled 36 patients undergoing aSCT.

pmc-12469826.title: Key Features of Culturally Inclusive, -Affirming and Contextually Relevant Mental Health Care and Healing Practices with Black Canadians: A Scoping Review
pmc-12469826.creator: Sophie Yohani, Chloe Devereux
pmc-12469826.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Black Canadians are one of the fastest-growing groups in Canada, with 59% of this population comprising immigrants. Ongoing systemic racism and discrimination have serious consequences for the mental health of Black Canadians. While research and policy efforts to address the mental health needs of this population are ongoing, a greater understanding of the healing practices relevant to this diverse population is needed.

pmc-12527171.title: Impact of group antenatal care on lactational amenorrhea method awareness and knowledge: A cluster randomized control trial
pmc-12527171.creator: Theresa Norpeli Lanyo, John E. O. Williams, Bidisha Ghosh, Veronica E. A. Apetorgbor, Vida A. Kukula, Ruth Zielinski, Elizabeth Awini, Cheryl A. Moyer, Jody Lori
pmc-12527171.description: High fertility rates in low and middle-income countries (LMICs), especially in sub-Saharan Africa and Ghana, lead to closely spaced pregnancies and contribute to high maternal and infant morbidity and mortality. Family planning remains critical for reducing rapid repeat and unwanted pregnancies, thus improving the health and survival outcomes.

pmc-12556575.title: Capacity-development on equity and diversity in a multinational European project
pmc-12556575.creator: I Hussein, M Nousiainen, S Kytö, T Spadea, B Armocida, B Formenti, N Skogberg
pmc-12556575.description: BackgroundReducing social inequities in health requires integrating equity, diversity, and inclusion from the start of program and policy development. Integrating these principles require structured capacity-development. The EU co-funded Joint Action on Cardiovascular Diseases and Diabetes (JACARDI) is an unprecedented collaboration of 21 countries and 142 pilot projects.

pmc-12562569.title: Factors Influencing the Colostrum’s Microbiota: A Systematic Review of the Literature
pmc-12562569.creator: Aimilia Tzani, Nikoleta Aikaterini Xixi, Rozeta Sokou, Eleni Karapati, Zoi Iliodromiti, Paraskevi Volaki, Styliani Paliatsiou, Nikoletta Iacovidou, Theodora Boutsikou, Daniele Zama
pmc-12562569.description: Background/Objectives: Human colostrum plays a crucial role in early microbial colonization, immune development, and gut health of newborns. Its microbiota is highly dynamic and influenced by numerous factors, yet the determinants remain poorly understood. This systematic review aims to investigate the composition of colostrum microbiota and the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that influence its diversity and abundance.
